# tfcensus mcp

mcp runs a Model Context Protocol server on stdin and stdout, for agents such as Claude Code.
Logs go to stderr. Each tool returns the JSON envelope the matching command prints with
--format json:

```text
units           tfcensus report units --index <file>
inventory       tfcensus report inventory --index <file>
whois           tfcensus whois --index <file> <arn|id>... (no --live, no accounts)
scan_summary    tfcensus report scan [--from <file>]
audit_findings  tfcensus report audit --from <file>
drift_summary   tfcensus report drift --from <file>
```

The tools answer from saved files only. They never call AWS, start terragrunt or terraform,
read a state, run a plan, or write a file, and move apply, rollback and mark-applied are not
tools. Run the commands that collect (inventory --save-index, scan, audit, drift) yourself,
and pass their output with the flags below. A tool whose file wasn't given fails with a
message naming the flag. scan\_summary without --scan reads the newest scan cache snapshot and
applies the config's ownership rules; a snapshot older than cache.ttl comes with a warning.
The files are read again on every call, so a new run is picked up without a restart.

Two prompts tell the agent which tools to call and to cite unit paths, addresses, rule IDs
and ARNs: triage\_drift \[unit\] sorts drift into revert, adopt and investigate, and
explain\_unmanaged \[account\] \[type\] explains the unmanaged resources of the last scan.
Claude Code offers them as /mcp\_\_tfcensus\_\_triage\_drift and /mcp\_\_tfcensus\_\_explain\_unmanaged.
Neither asks for attribute values. tfcensus has no built-in LLM call; for a summary in CI see
https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/guides/ai-summary.

A result over --max-result-bytes (default 50,000, Claude Code's limit for showing a result
to the model) is split. The envelope then has a page field, and the agent passes
page.next\_cursor back to the same tool for the rest. Double-managed and unmanaged resources
and high-severity findings come first. A cursor lasts 15 minutes after its last use.

## Usage

```sh
tfcensus mcp [flags]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Description | Type | Default | Values | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--audit` | audit JSON for audit\_findings | string |  |  |  |  |
| `--drift` | drift JSON for drift\_summary | string |  |  |  |  |
| `--index` | state index from tfcensus inventory --save-index, for units, inventory and whois | string |  |  |  |  |
| `--max-result-bytes` | split results larger than this many bytes of JSON into pages; 0 never splits | int | `50000` |  |  |  |
| `--scan` | scan JSON for scan\_summary (default: the newest scan cache snapshot) | string |  |  |  |  |

The [global flags](/cli/global-flags) work with every command.

## Output formats

This command ignores `--format`.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The command finished. With --fail-on, nothing matched. |
| 1 | The command failed: a read, a write, a child process or a check failed. |
| 2 | Wrong usage: an unknown command or flag, a bad value or argument, an invalid config file, or a prompt with no terminal. |
| 130 | Interrupted by Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or a cancelled context. |

All codes are listed on the [exit codes](/reference/exit-codes) page.

## Examples

```sh
tfcensus inventory --save-index ~/.cache/tfcensus/index.json.zst
claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope local tfcensus -- tfcensus mcp --index ~/.cache/tfcensus/index.json.zst
tfcensus mcp --index index.json.zst --scan scan.json --audit audit.json --drift drift.json
```
